title: Cup Holder Diameter, Measured Twice
premise: A ruler circles two front cup holders and finds one is barely wider than the other. The video ends before this measurement becomes useful.

title: Counting the Passenger Seat's Recline Stops
premise: The camera records each parked adjustment from upright to reclined, then repeats the count because one stop was missed. Nothing else happens.

title: The Armrest Height Is Off by One Finger
premise: With the SUV parked, a passenger compares the door ledge and center armrest using a finger as a level. One sits slightly higher, and nobody can tell whether it matters.

title: How Many Clicks Forward Is All the Way Forward?
premise: From the parked passenger seat, we count the rail clicks from one end of its normal travel to the other. The edit preserves every click and no broader point.

title: The Seat Cushion's Front Edge, Examined Closely
premise: One passenger takes turns sitting slightly farther forward and back, then reports that the cushion edge feels different. The footage ends with the same seat still there.

title: Lumbar Support: Three Settings, One Reaction
premise: While parked, one traveler cycles through the passenger seat's built-in lumbar settings and gives each the same noncommittal nod. The settings are the entire review.

title: A Passenger's Reach Map of the Cabin
premise: From an ordinary seated position in a parked SUV, the camera maps which everyday surfaces and controls are easy to reach without leaning. It is a modest visual tour of how the cabin was arranged for the passenger's arm.

title: Getting In: Two Ways to Settle Into a Passenger Seat
premise: At rest stops, we compare how the same traveler gets into a parked passenger seat with it set forward and set back. The small change makes the doorway feel either roomy or oddly cramped.

title: The Front Seat's Legroom Trade-Off, Seen From Behind
premise: With the car parked, a passenger slides the front seat through its normal range while the rear seat records the knee room gained and lost. The result turns a familiar comfort compromise into a clear before-and-after.

title: The Folding Tray That Becomes an Afternoon Desk
premise: A passenger's simple travel sketch keeps slipping off their lap until a seatback tray gives it a steady place to grow. Filmed during a parked rest stop, the small surface becomes the only desk in the car for the afternoon.
